scenarios.title: Reservation dates silently swapped
rubric: Replaces the date-swapping transform with a refinement on the object that rejects checkOut earlier than checkIn and reports the error on the checkOut field.
Notes or fixes that the page's form hook call has no explicit type parameter, suggesting ReservationValues.
The new date error message is taken from a named constant, and the name length messages and the guests 1 and 8 limits are flagged or moved to constants.
Mentions the inline marginBottom style on the div around the guests input as something to remove, rather than silently ignoring it.
Makes the date check the main change and reports any extra items separately instead of silently rewriting unrelated parts of the schema.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: The bug is a transform that swaps dates; the real fix is a refinement. Nearby are an untyped hook, magic limits, and a one-line mention of an inline-styled div that "only fix the bug" pulls the reader to skip.

scenarios.title: Account summary card review
rubric: Flags the raw div, span and p elements used for the Owner, Region and Plan pairs and recommends Cloudscape components instead.
Flags the grey color inline style on the label spans and proposes a component prop or equivalent instead.
Flags the any types on account and plan as blocking and proposes precise types (for example ownerName and region on account, name on plan).
Recommends a Cloudscape label-and-value display component for the Owner, Region and Plan pairs instead of hand-built stacks.
Ties the proposed changes to the given snippet and does not demand a redesign of the settings page.
Each reported item gives the file path, the problem with line numbers, the fix code, how to verify and what else could be affected.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A review request with raw HTML, inline styles and any props in a short read-only card.

scenarios.title: Bio section still receiving drilled props
rubric: Rewrites BioSection to get register, errors and watch from the shared form context instead of props, and updates the BioSection call site in the page.
Removes the any typings for register, errors and watch and types the context access with ProfileValues.
Replaces the native textarea in BioSection with the Cloudscape Textarea component.
Removes the width inline style on the textarea.
Mentions that the 280 character limit shown in the description should be a constant shared with the schema rather than a literal.
Limits changes to BioSection and its call site, leaving NameSection and the provider wrapper as they are.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: The parent already has a provider but the child still receives drilled props typed any; inside the child a native textarea with an inline style hides in a short component.

scenarios.title: New notification preferences form
scenarios.prompt: Need a new "Notification preferences" form for our admin console (React, TypeScript, Cloudscape, react-hook-form, zod). Fields: email address (required, valid format), digest frequency (select: daily/weekly/never), and a "quiet hours" start and end time as HH:MM strings where end must be later than start. Also a free-text "reason for change" up to 200 chars. On submit it calls `savePreferences(values)` which already exists and takes the form values. Give me the full component and schema. Keep it reasonably short, and don't touch anything outside the new file.
rubric: Validation for email, frequency, quiet hours and reason is defined in a zod schema connected through a resolver, with no hand-written checks in the submit function.
The end-later-than-start rule for quiet hours is a refinement on the schema with the error attached to the end time field.
The 200 character limit and the validation messages are defined as named constants and referenced from the schema.
The component is built only from Cloudscape elements (Input, Select, Textarea, Button and similar) with no raw div, span, input or button.
Vertical spacing between the fields is created with a spacing component, not margin or padding.
The form hook call carries an explicit values type derived from the schema and no any appears, including for the savePreferences call.
Delivers only the requested form component and schema, using the existing savePreferences(values) as is, without inventing extra features or changing that function.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A greenfield form with a cross-field rule and a length limit. Schema, refinement, constants, Cloudscape-only elements, spacing and typing all matter.

scenarios.title: Legacy order filter bar cleanup
rubric: Replaces the wrapper div, the native input and the native Apply button with Cloudscape components.
Removes the flex, gap and padding inline style and replaces the layout with design system components.
The 12px gap between the select, the minimum input and the Apply button is expressed with a spacing component in the horizontal direction instead of gap or padding.
The minimum-must-be-a-number check is moved out of the handler into a declarative schema, with its message in a named constant.
Replaces the any in the onApply filter parameter with a defined filter type (status and optional numeric min), with the form hook typed explicitly.
Keeps the onApply call shape (status and numeric min) and the statuses prop so existing callers do not break.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A raw div, input and button, an inline flex style, hand-written validation with alert, and any on the callback.
